summary: This article explains how green plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make their own sugary food in their leaves, giving off the oxygen that people and animals breathe.
introduce: Show the three key terms on the board and ask students to rate each one: “I know it,” “I have seen it,” or “It is new.” Tell them to watch for these words in “Photosynthesis: How Plants Make Food” and use clues around them to understand their meaning.

keyTerms.def: the way green plants use sunlight to make their own food
the green material in leaves that catches light from the sun
a gas in the air that people and animals breathe out

challengeTerms.def: a tiny part inside a plant cell where photosynthesis takes place
a living thing, such as a plant, that makes its own food
tiny openings on a leaf that let gases in and out

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that plants are the most important living things on Earth? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why people and animals depend on photosynthesis.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review photosynthesis, chlorophyll, and carbon dioxide, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use chloroplast, producer, and stomata in a short paragraph that teaches the class one of the terms with their own example.
